description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (relayed by JSON) from the JSON machine-code study (fz vs BEAM JIT, lldb single-step traces). Study files: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/ebbfffd8-2561-4da7-bcda-f9a316d00a1e/scratchpad/jsonasm/.

Evidence: 15 of ~25 instructions in an inline allocation are five read-modify-writes to process stat offsets (0x160, 0x170, 0x178, 0x1b0, 0x1b8; runtime/src/heap/mod.rs:108-111: total.allocs, total.bytes, continuation.allocs, continuation.bytes, ...), on every continuation and every box. Source: place_cont_closure and the alloc path in src/compiler2/native_codegen/closure.rs.

Constraints (GC, from origin/develop): the reader is fz_process_heap_alloc_stats (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:108); 56 fixtures pin *_allocs counts (e.g. 01592 list_cons_allocs == 0), so counts stay exact. Deriving from bump distance per block, or counting on the refill path, gives bytes but not per-object or per-kind counts, so neither keeps the counts exact. fz-9x7.16's in_use/idle figures come from the block pool (pool_footprint / Footprint), not HeapAllocStats, and are unaffected.

Options that keep counts exact: (a) the compiler sums each straight-line region's allocations by kind and size and emits one add per counter per region instead of per object; (b) the stats become test-only (needs a user ruling on what production observes).

Measurement first: how many inline allocations share a region on msg and enum. Then a page (GC offers review).

comments.text: Bugs and Cleanup's listing: the five allocation-statistics read-modify-writes cost 15 instructions per allocation, plus one on each frame given back. Binary Handling measured the same thing independently: <<byte>> inline is 78 instructions with the counters and 63 without, more than the allocation itself (about 8).

title: Allocation statistics leave the inline allocation path
